mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to compressed credit spreads and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: In high-rate regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the Fed cuts rates within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS growth is not accompanied by UNRATE declines, or when labor momentum reverses, 60-day forward returns show no significant improvement over the prior 60 days (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates resilient consumer demand supporting equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth >= 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth does not persist or is offset by simultaneous supply shocks, with 20-day returns not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% in a month followed by a decline in the prior month signals a supply-side shock that typically precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month increase > 5% followed by a decline in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 5-day windows following such INDPRO patterns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the US inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days as the market anticipates rate hikes that dampen growth prospects.
failure_condition: Inflation remains below 3% for 60 days after the trigger, with S&P 500 20-day returns returning to positive mean (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for 10 consecutive months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects labor market tightness that supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: UNRATE re-enters the 6–8% range before the 60-day window ends, with forward returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (proxy: HOUST) above 2% along with increasing consumer confidence (proxy: not available in catalog, so omit interaction) predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 return as it signals sustained demand momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Retail sales growth reverses or remains flat, with 20-day returns failing to beat the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over the same month suggests a dual labor-supply shock that increases risk premia and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 20-day windows following such dual declines (p > 0.05).
